key.name: external-display-count
key.summary: Number of external displays the extension can control
key.description: Written by the extension for the preferences window, which runs in its own process and cannot see the displays. Not meant to be changed by hand.

key.name: group-displays
key.description: One brightness and one contrast slider apply the same level to every external display. Only has an effect with two or more of them.

key.name: show-contrast
key.description: When disabled, only brightness sliders are shown.

key.name: limit-minimum-brightness
key.description: Keeps the brightness sliders from going below 1%, since some displays turn the backlight off at 0 and leave no way to see the slider. When disabled, they go all the way down.

key.name: slider-placement
key.description: With "tile" the sliders are in a Quick Settings tile with a menu. With "inline" the brightness sliders sit below the brightness slider of GNOME, without a tile. "inline" only has an effect on the GNOME Shell versions it was checked on.

key.name: inline-position
key.summary: Where the inline sliders go relative to the brightness slider of GNOME
key.description: Only used when the sliders are placed "inline". With "above" they sit right above the brightness slider of GNOME, with "below" right below it.

key.name: enable-auto-rotate
key.description: When enabled, displays that report an orientation over DDC/CI get an Auto Rotate switch in the Displays menu. When disabled, no switches are shown and the orientation of the displays is never read, whatever auto-rotate-displays says. Off by default, so that the extension behaves as before auto-rotate was added until it is turned on.

key.name: auto-rotate-displays
key.description: Model and serial, as "model#serial", of every display that is rotated when it is turned. Only displays with an orientation sensor that report it over DDC/CI (VCP 0xAA), such as some portable monitors, can rotate. Set with the Auto Rotate switches in the Displays menu.

key.name: auto-rotate-interval
key.description: How often the orientation of the displays with auto-rotate on is read. DDC/CI only answers when asked, so a shorter interval rotates sooner at the cost of more traffic on the display bus.
